text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Greek Cypriot press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Confusion on stock market over trading in cement factories. Stock exchange suspends trading in Vassiliko cement and Cyprus Cement Works for two days.
- Co-operative commissioner is asked to investigate claims the Mayor of Aglandjia suburb of Nicosia paid 1,200 pounds out of local co-op fund to sponsor a chat show on a radio station.
- Shipping magnate delays Cyprus Airways plane for an hour, demanding his staff be upgraded to business class without paying a penny.
- Talks stall as doctors and nurses strike.
- Socialist Edek leader Vassos Lyssarides calls for the British bases to go.
- Sacked board member of the state-run electricity authority accuses MP Christos Pourgourides of the ruling Disy party of abuse of power.
- Cypriots are being fired from their jobs at British bases.
- Major political debate breaks out over British statements that Cyprus's accession to the EU would be difficult, if not impossible, before a solution to the Cyprus problem.
- Workers threaten strikes in Paphos hotels over the employment of foreigners.
- Civil servants union Pasidy and Finance Minister Christodoulos Christodoulou sharpen their knives over nurses and doctors demands.
- Cypriot students came bottom of the list of a worldwide study of science and mathematics.
- Flyovers over Cyprus of fighter jets are to be suspended for one year.
